newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures posted their largest one-day gain since June 28 after benign French and U.S. inflation figures bolstered hopes of an intervention rate cut and calmed fears U.S. interest rate would rise on September 24.
French bonds outpaced German bonds all along the curve and the 10-year spread, using the 7.25 percent 2006 bond, turned negative. The OAT yield fell 10 basis points to 6.20 percent.

Traders said although there had been good buying by non-residents on Friday, partly amid a re-evaluation of the risk of social unrest in France, some consolidation at the beginning of next week ahead of the French budget presentation was likely.
The September bond future surged through several resistance levels to settle at 125.16, up 80 centimes on the day, while the December future settled at 123.64.

A surprise 0.2 to 0.3 percent drop in August French consumer prices gave OATs a boost at the open before a U.S. bond rally sent European bond markets surging higher in the afternoon with large volumes of futures contracts being traded.
"It wasn't an historic high, it was an hysteric high," said a trader at a French brokerage.
Analysts said a lowering of call money next week now looked likely with some banking on an intervention rate cut soon.

Notwithstanding the possibility of slight underperformance at the time of the budget presentation on September 18, bond analysts were focusing on the fact some domestic investors had cash ready to invest.
The flood of coupon payments and redemptions due in October and December was also being cited as a positive factor for the French bond market.

Ciaran O'Hagan, bond analyst at JP Morgan, estimated total coupon repayments and redemptions would outstrip projected government and unswapped corporate supply by 80 billion francs during the October and November.
The franc broke through 3.41 briefly late on Friday to hit a high of 3.4094 per mark, up from the day's low of 3.4160.
The positive tone in the currency market and the revival of interest rate cut hopes gave PIBOR contracts a boost. The December contract rallied to settle up nine basis points at 96.14.
